## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s21. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code, run by the pipeline from sealed argument vectors. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that runs on each arm's output without access to the arm's identity. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents and by the processes of arms and evaluator. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. Declared residual risks, which no rule below removes: the evaluator reads the arm's output files by design, so file names or content under `out/` that identify the program can reach it (the sealed `evaluate.sh` bytes make any dependence on them auditable after the run); and state of shared hardware (device memory, caches, timing) is not cleared between parts. - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. - `commands`: 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. The pipeline runs them (see Evaluate); the arm's adapter only prepares. - `env`: null or an object mapping names that match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and do not start with `CMP_` to strings; set for the arm's commands. - Placeholders, in command and `env` strings only: `{input}` (the input id), `{run}`, `{out}` (the absolute paths of the invocation's `run/` and `out/`) and `{spec:

}` with `

` a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input's `spec`, which must resolve in every input's `spec` to a string (inserted as is) or a finite number (inserted as `json.dumps` writes it). `{{` and `}}` stand for literal braces; any other `{` or `}` makes the design invalid. Substitution replaces every occurrence and is not repeated on its result. - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration). - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format, select}`: a logical result each arm, or the evaluator, writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers). `select` is null (the whole content) or, for `bytes` and `text_numbers` only, a Python `re` pattern with at least one capturing group: the content is read as UTF-8 with replacement, and the selected content is every group of every match of `re.finditer(select, text, re.MULTILINE)`, in order (an unmatched group as the empty string), joined by `"\n"`; `format` then applies to the selected content (`bytes` to its UTF-8 encoding). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. ## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s23. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code, run by the pipeline from sealed argument vectors. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that runs on each arm's output without access to the arm's identity. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents and by the processes of arms and evaluator. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. Declared residual risks, which no rule below removes: the evaluator reads the arm's output files by design, so file names or content under `out/` that identify the program can reach it (the sealed `evaluate.sh` bytes make any dependence on them auditable after the run); state of shared hardware (device memory, caches, timing) is not cleared between parts; and a harness script that disobeys the rule that only `fetch_private.sh` handles the evaluator's private data can leave a transformed copy of them (an archive, a re-encoding, a derived file) where the arm part can read it, which the byte-identity check of Separated users step 7 does not detect (`setup.sh` and its repairs are kept in `A/harness/` and the stage's receipts, so such a copy is auditable after the run). - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. - `commands`: 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. The pipeline runs them (see Evaluate); the arm's adapter only prepares. - `env`: null or an object mapping names that match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and do not start with `CMP_` to strings; set for the arm's commands. - Placeholders, in command and `env` strings only: `{input}` (the input id), `{run}`, `{out}` (the absolute paths of the invocation's `run/` and `out/`) and `{spec:

}` with `

` a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input's `spec`, which must resolve in every input's `spec` to a string (inserted as is) or a finite number (inserted as `json.dumps` writes it). `{{` and `}}` stand for literal braces; any other `{` or `}` makes the design invalid. Substitution replaces every occurrence and is not repeated on its result. - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration). - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format, select}`: a logical result each arm, or the evaluator, writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers). `select` is null (the whole content) or, for `bytes` and `text_numbers` only, a Python `re` pattern with at least one capturing group: the content is read as UTF-8 with replacement, and the selected content is every group of every match of `re.finditer(select, text, re.MULTILINE)`, in order (an unmatched group as the empty string), joined by `"\n"`; `format` then applies to the selected content (`bytes` to its UTF-8 encoding). Several outputs may select different parts of the same file, each with its own comparison and tolerance. - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source, reduce, expect_count}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` or `"sealed_extraction"`. - `trusted_wall`: the invocation's wall seconds: the adapter's wall plus its commands' walls, plus the evaluator's wall when the design has an evaluator. `reduce` and `expect_count` are null. - `sealed_extraction`: read from fetched files by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run, reduced as the design states. `reduce` `"first"`, `"max"` or `"value_at_max_key"`; `expect_count` null or a positive integer, the number of matched values the rule must find. - `evaluator`: null or exactly `{what, spec, timeout_s}`: a published, pinned program that reads one arm's output for one input, with data that only it may read, and writes evaluation files. `what` a non-empty string; `spec` any JSON value (program, pin, command, and where its private data come from); `timeout_s` null or a positive integer. - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `bootstrap_resamples` an integer from 1000 to 1000000; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison.
